div.head: Romscot 1
div.ab: Romgescot sý agifen on sanctus Petrus mæssedæg ǽr undern æfter middesumera.
Romschoss werde entrichtet an dem nach Mittsommer [fallenden] Fest des heiligen Petrus [1. Aug.] vor Mittag.
Let Rome-scot be paid on the feast of St Peter [1 August] that falls after midsummer, before noon.
St Peter's pence is to be paid before Terce on St Peter's day after midsummer [1 August].

note.label: verbally quoted
note.quote: The sixty shilling/twelvefold restitution penalty was demanded by Ine for non-payment of Church-scot, and his law was verbally quoted here

note.label: contrast
note.quote: Edgar … stipulated a much stiffer penalty for non-compliance: the fine was doubled, restitution multiplied by thirty not twelve

note.label: adaptation of, echoing verbally
note.quote: the text is self-evidently an adaptation of Ine's law on church-scot to the extent of echoing it verbally

div.note: U: translator unrecorded: check; MS G (Cotton Nero A I, f. 47, after the Af–Ine rubrics, same hand c. 1060). Liebermann dates it about 1050 and wonders if it is a private note of local law (G elsewhere has a text of Kentish origin). Clause number standardised from ‘Romscot 1’.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.1050; before 959 (Wormald)”, now “c.1050 (Liebermann); before 959 (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.1050 (Liebermann); before 959 (Wormald)”, now “c.1050 (Liebermann, I p. 474); before 959 (Wormald, MEL p. 368)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “G 474; German 474”; 2 rows of Romscot)
